title: Following Delegation Traces to Study Human Oversight in Interaction with Multimodal AI
abstract: arXiv:2610.21948v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As multimodal AI systems are becoming our everyday thought partners, the shift towards studying how users transfer control to these systems becomes especially urgent. In this paper, we report an overview of findings from an online study with n=56 AI-literate participants and 392 Video Question Answering trials. After inspecting each multimodal AI response, participants rated task-specific trust and selected one of three intended policies for an analogous future task: reject AI assistance, use it with verification, or delegate fully to the AI. Within participants, post-interaction trust strongly predicted the user's delegation choices (OR=14.97, 95% CI [7.14,31.37]). Trust and delegation nevertheless remained distinct. Verification was the dominant policy and often co-occurred with high trust. translated_title: 追踪委托轨迹以研究人与多模态AI交互中的人类监督
translated_abstract: 随着多模态AI系统日益成为我们日常思考的伙伴，研究用户如何将控制权转移给这些系统变得尤为紧迫。在本文中，我们报告了一项在线研究的主要发现，该研究共有56名具备AI素养的参与者，进行了392次视频问答试验。在检查每个多模态AI的回应后，参与者对任务特定的信任度进行评分，并针对类似的未来任务从三种意图策略中选择一种：拒绝AI辅助、在使用时进行验证、或完全委托给AI。在参与者内部，交互后的信任度强烈预测了用户的委托选择（OR=14.97，95% CI [7.14, 31.37]）。然而，信任与委托仍然是两个相互独立的构念。验证性使用是最主要的策略，且经常与高信任度同时出现。在调整了瞬时信任和参与者层面信任之后，委托仍随任务顺序的增加而上升（OR=1.22，95% CI [1.02, 1.45]），这表明……
tldr: 该研究通过56名参与者392次视频问答试验发现，信任虽强烈预测用户对AI的委托选择，但信任与委托是相互独立的构念——验证性使用才是主流策略，且委托倾向会随任务顺序独立增长。
en_tdlr: A study of 56 participants across 392 video question-answering trials reveals that trust and delegation remain distinct constructs—trust strongly predicts delegation choices, yet verification is the dominant policy and delegation independently increases with task order.
